input: "Mostly for myself. I'd like an audience, but perhaps one that has already been fed." I smile at Seraphel and Caelindra. "I'll bring something short tomorrow, if you'd like to hear it." Then to Rashid and Ashara: "I can't provide a south market, but come to the common room tomorrow afternoon if you like. Bring your writing, or bring nothing. We could try an hour without an assessment." I finish dinner and join the proposed game afterward. "For tonight, someone will have to explain Bastions before I embarrass the house."
output:
Rashid’s brows lift. “An afternoon without assessment? I’ll come, if you tell me the hour. I reserve the right to judge any pastries.”

“I train through fourth bell,” Ashara says. “Afterward, I can bring nothing with distinction.”

Caelindra turns her wineglass by the stem. “And the promised reading occurs in this common room, presumably?”

Seraphel beams.

“Where Rowan reads, I’ll gladly sit;  
I swear not to improve a bit.”

“An alarming promise from a poet,” Caelindra murmurs.

Dinner ends with honeyed plums and a cheese sharp enough to numb your tongue. Aldric excuses himself for evening prayers, denying that his departure has anything to do with Bastions encouraging deceit.

“He lost last week,” Rashid explains after the door shuts.

The game emerges from a cabinet beneath the Garvey portraits. Its board unfolds into seven painted fortresses joined by removable roads. Seven sets of pieces fill the box: glass, bone, iron, wood, silver, stone—and brass, tarnished almost brown. Rashid wipes the brass envoys on his handkerchief before setting them before you without comment.

“The object,” he says, “is to have your envoys admitted into four bastions when the truce bell rings.”

“Three and the central keep also suffice,” Caelindra says.

“If the keep is uncontested.”

“It will not be,” Ashara adds. “Everyone negotiates simultaneously. Agreements last precisely as long as stated.”

Thessaly arranges her black stone gates. “Promises made within the game remain promises. Choose your words deliberately.”

Before your first round has officially begun, Rashid offers safe passage along his western road in exchange for one future gate-opening. Caelindra immediately slides a silver bridge toward your brass fortress.

“Passage for this round,” she says. “No tribute. I would prefer that vel Amara not acquire a beginner before the pieces are warm.”

“I am teaching,” Rashid protests.

“You are purchasing.”

Ashara folds her arms behind your chair. “Reject both until you understand the map.”

Across the board, Ysolde quietly occupies the central keep while everyone is looking at you.
